title: [internal] Match Caddy WebSocket defaults; 256 KiB cap disconnects LiveView

labels.name: internal request fixed
labels.description: Internal request resolved in a published Gaoxy release

body:
**Requesting repo:** gsmlg-opt/Synapsis on branch `main` (baseline `f97ea32c3aae7e490b4484fa508bc60656e2be67`, with uncommitted Gaoxy integration changes).

**Severity:** needed — the default breaks existing session pages; an explicit local service-budget override currently restores service.

Please update Gaoxy's effective default WebSocket payload behavior to match **Caddy: no default transport-imposed data-frame/message payload ceiling**, with bounded streaming buffers and explicit configurable limits. This request concerns WebSocket payload capacity, including the service-budget interaction that currently reduces otherwise valid Phoenix messages to 256 KiB.

### Observed failure

With `gaoxy`, `gaoxy_http` and `gaoxy_websock_adapter` **0.12.1**, Phoenix **1.8.16** and LiveView **1.2.13**:

- HTTP health checks and small LiveView pages succeed.
- A session page successfully upgrades its WebSocket, then immediately receives close **1011**, with an empty reason, when the initial LiveView render is sent. Phoenix repeatedly reconnects.
- The actual initial LiveView message is **313,781 bytes**. The same failure occurs through loopback and the LAN address.
- A separate real TCP/WebSocket regression, without sessions or LLM/provider calls, reproduces the same **1011** with a **300 KiB / 307,200-byte** server reply.

### Why the effective default is 256 KiB

The default HTTP/1 service has `limits.max_bytes = 1_048_576`. `Gaoxy.HTTP.WebSocket.start/2` clips both frame/message ceilings to `service_limits.max_bytes / 4`, yielding **262,144 bytes**, even though WebSockAdapter supplies a **10,000,000-byte** frame ceiling. An oversized outgoing callback fails with `:output_limit` and closes with 1011.

The same defaults and clamp are still present by source inspection in current main, `e435c05b08d7cbdb0e3c02ee585f23ddc8b9316f` (Gaoxy HTTP 0.12.2). The network reproduction above was run on the installed 0.12.1 packages.

- [Default shared service budget](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy/blob/e435c05b08d7cbdb0e3c02ee585f23ddc8b9316f/apps/gaoxy/lib/gaoxy/config.ex#L5)
- [WebSocket defaults and service-budget clipping](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy/blob/e435c05b08d7cbdb0e3c02ee585f23ddc8b9316f/apps/gaoxy_http/lib/gaoxy/http/websocket.ex#L24-L108)
- [Outgoing payload accounting and output_limit](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/gaoxy/blob/e435c05b08d7cbdb0e3c02ee585f23ddc8b9316f/apps/gaoxy_http/lib/gaoxy/http/websocket.ex#L405-L427)

Related: #6 fixed how an omitted message limit follows an explicitly selected frame limit. This report covers the remaining **default HTTP/1 service budget** and **server-to-client** output failure, rather than that earlier configured-limit issue.

### Caddy baseline

Verified against Caddy **v2.11.7**, commit `72dd0fb067f6d7826c7f79907670ba4a713bfe37`:

- The [official reverse_proxy documentation](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy#streaming) describes WebSocket upgrades becoming bidirectional tunnels.
- Its [implementation copies opaque bytes with io.CopyBuffer in both directions](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/72dd0fb067f6d7826c7f79907670ba4a713bfe37/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/streaming.go#L686-L705), without a data-frame/message payload-size check.
- The [default 32 KiB streaming buffers](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/72dd0fb067f6d7826c7f79907670ba4a713bfe37/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/streaming.go#L718-L738) are reused transfer buffers, not message limits.

Caddy therefore has **no numeric default WebSocket payload cap to copy**. The requested parity is its default payload behavior; application-level limits may still apply independently.

### Minimal reproduction

Run `elixir repro.exs` in an otherwise empty directory. This starts only a temporary Gaoxy listener:

```elixir
Mix.install([
  {:gaoxy_http, "== 0.12.1"},
  {:websock_adapter, "== 0.12.1", hex: :gaoxy_websock_adapter, override: true}
])

defmodule SizeProbe.Socket do
  @behaviour WebSock
  def init(state), do: {:ok, state}
  def handle_in({"large", opcode: :text}, state),
    do: {:push, {:text, String.duplicate("x", 300 * 1024)}, state}
  def handle_info(_, state), do: {:ok, state}
end

defmodule SizeProbe.Plug do
  def init(options), do: options
  def call(conn, _) do
    conn
    |> WebSockAdapter.upgrade(SizeProbe.Socket, nil, [])
    |> Plug.Conn.halt()
  end
end

{:ok, listener} = Gaoxy.HTTP.start_link(
  id: :size_probe,
  plug: {SizeProbe.Plug, []},
  ip: {127, 0, 0, 1},
  port: 0
)
IO.inspect(Gaoxy.info(listener, :size_probe).local, label: "probe address")
Process.sleep(:infinity)
```

Save this client as `probe.mjs` and run `node probe.mjs ws://127.0.0.1:PORT/` with Node 22+ and the printed port:

```javascript
const ws = new WebSocket(process.argv[2]);
const timer = setTimeout(() => process.exit(2), 5000);
ws.addEventListener("open", () => ws.send("large"));
ws.addEventListener("message", ({data}) => {
  console.log("received bytes:", Buffer.byteLength(data));
  ws.close(1000);
});
ws.addEventListener("close", ({code, reason}) => {
  clearTimeout(timer);
  console.log("closed:", code, JSON.stringify(reason));
});
```

Current default: `closed: 1011 ""`, with no text reply. The handler retains only `nil`, so this reproduction does not trip the separate handler-state limit.

### Requested change / acceptance

1. Align default WebSocket payload behavior with Caddy, addressing the effective service-budget clamp as well as frame/message defaults. Ordinary Phoenix/LiveView messages above 256 KiB must work without application-specific budget overrides.
2. Keep explicit application-selected frame/message limits and resource controls configurable, documented and effective. Reusable transfer-buffer sizes should not become a hidden whole-message size cap.
3. Cover real socket tests for a 300 KiB server reply, the initial Phoenix/LiveView join reply, and continued heartbeat/traffic on the same connection. Also test explicitly configured limits.
4. Publish the change in the coordinated Gaoxy package cohort so downstream applications can remove their temporary budget overrides.

For comparison, Synapsis currently sets `http: [limits: %{max_bytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024}]`. This finite local workaround makes the isolated 300 KiB reply pass (length and hash checked), with ping/pong and subsequent echo on the same connection; the existing SSE transport regression also passes. After restarting, both browser addresses received the complete 313,781-byte LiveView render and stayed connected through multiple heartbeat cycles with no close/error events. This 64 MiB override is a temporary consumer setting, not a claimed Caddy default.
